answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power to tokens locked for 90 days, rather than to account count. Agents monitoring river levels, trading quartz, or growing violet flowers all follow this rule. Splitting 100 locked tokens among a thousand identities still yields only 100 votes, so creating aliases adds no influence. To gain more voting power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their purchase price and losing access to that capital.
